topic: Memory Hierarchy and Caching Strategies: Registers Disk
explanation: The memory hierarchy organizes storage based on speed and cost, ranging from the fastest, smallest CPU registers down through multi-level caches (L1/L2/L3), main DRAM, and finally to the slowest, largest magnetic or solid-state disk storage. Caching strategies exploit temporal and spatial locality by proactively moving frequently accessed data blocks into faster, lower-latency tiers. This mechanism minimizes the average memory access time (AMAT) by maximizing the cache hit rate. Effective program performance depends critically on optimizing data access patterns to leverage the high bandwidth and low latency of the upper hierarchy levels.
